text:
maria: Heads-up — apiserver 5xx spike in eu3 starting ~03:12 UTC. Controller-manager queue length growing and a bunch of GPU-onboard jobs stuck in Pending. Seeing k8s events about attach/detach timeouts.
ken: grabbing logs. any recent infra changes in eu3?
alex: I deployed a small kmod update earlier but only to a few nodes, not controlplane.
maria: looks like etcd kicked off compaction sweep at 03:12 and wal fsync latencies climbed. iops on the nvme spiked. metrics: etcd_wal_sync_duration_ms p95 -> 1200ms, disk_ops ~ 6200 iops for /var/lib/etcd.
sre-oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident PD12345 triggered: apiserver_5xx_rate_high (severity: high)
tim: can you paste the etcd warnings?
maria: logs:
```
2026-03-21T03:12:11Z etcdserver: starting compaction revision 8292345
2026-03-21T03:12:12Z rafthttp: dropped incoming heartbeat from leader=3 rev=8292346; latency 1100ms
2026-03-21T03:12:14Z etcdserver: WAL sync took 1.21s; slowing apply
```
ken: that rafthttp line explains leader election jitter. leader-election events are spiking on apiserver pods.
sophie: controller-manager logs show lease renew failures: "failed to update leader lease: context deadline exceeded"
alex: provisioning side-effects: provisioner is retrying GPU attach and throwing 502/504 to apiserver in the retry path, which amplifies the apiserver load.
maria: kubectl get pods -n kube-system shows many apiserver replicas restarting, imagepull backoff? no, restarts from liveness probes due to timeouts.
sophie: temporary mitigation: lower controller-manager leaseDuration+renewDeadline? risky. maybe scale up apiserver replicas in eu3 for headroom.
tim: scaling apiserver might help short-term. also throttle provisioner concurrency to reduce attach storms. suggestion: set PROVISIONER_CONCURRENCY=4 for eu3 pool.
alex: agreed. i'm patching a canary to reduce concurrency and increasing apiserver HPA max from 6->10 (eu3 only).
deploy-bot: deployment/cluster-provisioner updated: replicaCount=2 -> 1 (concurrency-patch)
ken: also let's check disk saturation on etcd nodes. if compaction sweep is causing runaway writes, we can pause scheduled compaction or move to a different storage tier for wal.
maria: pausing compaction now on leader: `ETCD_SNAPSHOT_COMPACT=false` (temp) — doing on a single leader node.
sophie: watch for DB growth — don't forget to re-enable and schedule to low-traffic window.
tim: iops relief visible: disk_ops down to ~1200 iops now, wal sync p95 -> 140ms. apiserver error rate falling.
ken: controller-manager queue length decreasing. GPU attach retries dropping.
alex: cost note — if we keep apiserver replica increase for >24h we'll use more reserved CPU/GPU-support resources in eu3; flagging to finance that this is mitigative.
maria: short postmortem items: 1) investigate why compaction sweep launched during high attach window (cron vs dynamic). 2) add backpressure to provisioner to honor apiserver 429s. 3) move etcd wal to provisioned NVMe FS with io1-like policy. 4) add a playbook entry to throttle GPU-onboard concurrency for region.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident PD12345 acknowledged by tim
ken: i'll open a ticket for storage changes and tag infra-storage. anyone want to draft the runbook edit?
sophie: i'll draft the runbook and drop it in #incidents after lunch. :+1:
maria: thanks team — keeping this thread for final notes. I'll update when we re-enable compaction (in low-traffic window).
deploy-bot: autoscaler: apiserver eu3 scaled 4 -> 9 replicas (by alex)
alex: apiserver error rate stabilized to baseline. closing PD when metrics hold for 15m.
maria: last check — controller-manager queue length normal, GPU-onboard backlog cleared. marking root cause as etcd compaction IO spike causing temporary raft latency and apiserver liveness timeouts.
ken: agreed. follow-ups: storage ticket, provisioner backpressure, runbook update.
maria: closing thread in 10m unless anything else pops up.
